tier_rationale: Manufacturer's own product page describes only physical controls and an LCD screen with no app, Bluetooth, or connectivity feature, and no FCC grant exists for the PM500 despite OMRON Healthcare holding 27 grants for other radio-equipped models (its wireless Bluetooth blood pressure monitors), establishing that the vendor files when it has a radio to declare.
the_unplug_test: There is nothing to unplug. The PM500 runs on 2 AAA batteries, you set intensity and mode with physical buttons, and the LCD on the unit itself shows the settings. It has no app, no pairing step, and no account of any kind — it cannot lose a feature to a server because it was never connected to one.

repairability.notes: Uses replaceable electrode pads (consumable, sold separately) and 2 AAA batteries; no teardown or parts-availability source checked.

sources.supports: Manufacturer product page: describes physical button controls and an 'Easy-to-read LCD', runs on 2 AAA batteries, and makes no mention of an app, Bluetooth, WiFi, or account of any kind for this model.

FCC ID search for grantee OMRON HEALTHCARE Co., Ltd. (grantee code Q6Z) lists 27 grants, all Bluetooth/BLE blood pressure monitors (HEM-series). No grant exists for the PM500 or any OMRON TENS/pain-management model, and the vendor demonstrably files grants for its own radio-equipped products, making the absence for this model meaningful.

open_questions: Current US price band not established.
Parts availability for the control unit itself (beyond consumable electrode pads) not checked.
notes: Fills an empty subcategory (TENS unit) in the health domain. OMRON also sells a 'Complete Wireless' Bluetooth+ECG blood pressure monitor (BP7900) and other connected lines, so this is a case of a single vendor selling both connected and unconnected product families side by side — the PM500 is the unconnected one.
